in_text_mentions: The omovertebral bone most frequently attached to the cervical spine at C6 (5 cases), followed by C7 (2 cases); the remaining 5 cases were at other levels with 2 or 3 cervical sections. In the majority of the shoulders, the omovertebral bone was tethered to the convexity of the infraspinous portion of the vertebral border, whereas in three shoulders, it anchored to the convexity of the mesoscapular portion. The morphology of the omovertebral bone was diverse. Most of the shapes were irregular (Figures 6a,b). Some exhibited rhomboid or cylindrical shapes (Figures 7a,7b).

in_text_mentions: The omovertebral bone most frequently attached to the cervical spine at C6 (5 cases), followed by C7 (2 cases); the remaining 5 cases were at other levels with 2 or 3 cervical sections. In the majority of the shoulders, the omovertebral bone was tethered to the convexity of the infraspinous portion of the vertebral border, whereas in three shoulders, it anchored to the convexity of the mesoscapular portion.
